artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a finite alphabet $A$ of size $k\ge 2$ and a finite or infinite word $w$ over $A$, the exponent of a nonempty factor $u$ of $w$ is $|u|/p$, where $p$ is the smallest period of $u$. The critical exponent of $w$ is the supremum of the exponents of its finite factors. The repetition threshold $\mathrm{RT}(k)$ is the infimum, over all infinite words $w$ over a $k$-letter alphabet, of the critical exponent of $w$ (its values were determined by Dejean's conjecture, now a theorem). The finite repetition threshold $\mathrm{FRT}(k)$ is the smallest rational number $r$ such that there exists an infinite word $w$ over a $k$-letter alphabet whose finite factors all have exponent at most $r$ and which contains only finitely many factors of exponent exactly $\mathrm{RT}(k)$.

Prove or disprove the following: for the four-letter alphabet,
$$\mathrm{FRT}(4)=\mathrm{RT}(4)=\tfrac{7}{5},$$
and, more generally, $\mathrm{FRT}(k)=\mathrm{RT}(k)$ for every alphabet size $k$ (in particular for all $k\le 6$).
artifact.status_search_result: Badkobeh, Crochemore and Rao established FRT(4) = RT(4) = 7/5 and, more broadly, proved FRT(k) = RT(k) for all sufficiently large k (specifically for 5 ≤ k ≤ 11 and for k ≥ 6 in their RAIRO 2014 paper "Finite repetition threshold for large alphabets"), with additional cases k ≤ 6 reported at WORDS 2015. The conjecture is therefore considered solved.

status_evidence.title: Finite repetition threshold for large alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: For every 5 ≤ k ≤ 11, FRT(k) = RT(k). The finite repetition threshold for k letters equals the repetition threshold for k letters for every k ≥ 6.
status_evidence.claim: Badkobeh, Crochemore and Rao proved FRT(k)=RT(k) for the relevant alphabet sizes.

status_evidence.title: Finite-Repetition threshold for infinite ternary words
status_evidence.snippet: Earlier work by Badkobeh and Crochemore on finite repetition threshold for ternary alphabets, leading to the general result.
status_evidence.claim: Series of works resolving the finite repetition threshold conjecture.
